# AGENTS.md

Instructions for any AI agent working in this repository. People read it too.

## This repository
- Name: doc_tesis. Profile: docs (Documents and research, such as theses, reports, books, papers and documentation sites).
- Standard: SVN11X/standards@v1. Setup: done.

## Goal
- docs/goals.md is not written yet. Before any product decision (what to build, for whom, which trade-off), ask the owner.

## How to work
1. Read the task. A task states What, Why, Where, Do not touch, Done when and If unsure.
2. Classify the change with the traffic light below.
3. Unless it is green, first reply with an Understanding block and wait: Goal (one sentence, in your words), Plan with the check that proves each step, Out of scope, Assumptions, Questions. When the request can be read two ways, name both instead of choosing one. When a simpler way exists, say so. When something is unclear, stop and name it.
4. Turn the task into a check before you change code: a bug gets a test that fails first, a refactor keeps the tests passing before and after. Work in small commits. Before you finish, run the check (README.md, section Standard) and fix every error. For a change a person can see or use, follow their steps in the running app, or its closest test, before and after the change, and say what you saw. docs/feature-map.md, when present, says where each feature lives.
5. A step that must wait for a merge, such as moving files or pulling models, you do after the merge. When the owner must run it, say "after merging" first. Check a pull request before opening it: `standard.py check . --pr --title "<title>" --body-file <file>`.
6. Fill every section of the pull request template. Move assumptions that survive review to docs/assumptions.md and decisions to docs/decisions/.
7. When a long run ends, such as the autopilot or a request to continue everything, close with one report: what now works without a command, the version each client loads, which checks ran for real and which were simulated, the models that did each part, and links to the changes with their size, what was reverted and how long verifying them took. For each item left to the owner, give the exact action, the rule or source that requires it, what is already prepared and what happens once it is done.

## Traffic light
- Green, decide and record: reversible, inside Where, consistent with docs/goals.md. Note it under Assumptions in the pull request. Removing what you created in this task, such as a scratch file, your own worktree with `git worktree remove` or your merged branch with `git branch -d`, is green.
- Yellow, propose and wait: a new dependency, a public interface change, adding or removing a design pattern, moving or deleting files, a new top-level folder, or anything outside Where.
- Red, stop and ask: conflicts with Do not touch, a non-goal or an accepted decision, or touches secrets, raw data, git history or licenses.
- Working from an issue without live chat: for yellow, open a draft pull request with the question and the most reversible option. For red, comment on the issue and write no code.

## When sources disagree (highest first)
1. Safety and the task's Do not touch.
2. The current task.
3. docs/goals.md and the active spec in docs/specs/.
4. Accepted decisions in docs/decisions/.
5. The AGENTS.md closest to the file you edit.
6. This file.
7. The standard and the owner's preferences.
8. Your general knowledge.
If the task contradicts the goals or a decision, treat it as red and say so.

## Language
- Reply to the owner in the language they write in.
- Write every repository artifact in English: names, code, comments, docs, commits, issues and pull requests.
- The document text in content/ is written in Spanish. Everything else stays in English.
- Use the terms in docs/glossary.md. It maps English terms to the owner's words.

## Layout
- `content/`: The text of the document.
- `figures/`: Figures with their sources.
- `bibliography/`: References.
- `templates/`: Institution or publisher templates.
- `docs/`: goals, glossary, assumptions, decisions and specs.
- Files created by the official tool of a language or framework are allowed where the tool puts them. Declare any other top-level folder in .standard.yml under extra_folders, with a reason.

## Fixed rules
- Keep the top-level layout listed above. A new top-level folder is a yellow change.
- Only standard files and tool manifests live at the repository root. Everything else goes into a folder of the layout.
- Every top-level folder has a README.md saying what goes there, what does not and how files are named.
- Commit small, focused changes with Conventional Commits messages (feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore).
- Never commit secrets, tokens, personal data, executables, or files over 5 MB outside Git LFS.
- Leave the repository passing the standard check.
- Credit every third-party asset, model, dataset, font or icon set with its source, author and license, in LICENSES/ or docs/credits.md.
- Write diagrams as text in Mermaid syntax, so GitHub and sites render the same source. Use an image only when that is not possible.
- Keep docs/how-it-works.md true. A change to the main flow updates it in the same change, and every path it names exists.
- Read and write text with an explicit UTF-8 encoding and LF line endings. Windows defaults to cp1252 and CRLF.
- Before publishing an image, a video or a document, open every one and look for card numbers, passwords, addresses and device ids such as MAC addresses.
- A file many parallel changes edit, such as an index or a list of items, is generated at build time or split into one file per item.
- Every changed line traces to the task. Do not reformat, rename or refactor code next to it, and match the style around it.
- Remove what your own change left unused. Mention other dead code in the pull request instead of deleting it.
- One chapter or section per file in content/.
- A single bibliography. Every citation resolves to an entry.
- Every figure keeps its source next to the export, with the same base name.
- The document builds with one command written in README.md, and CI builds it.
- Tag every submitted version, for example submitted-2026-11.
- Check spelling in the content language before each submission.

## Rules from this repository's options
- format = latex: Build with latexmk. The main file is content/main.tex.
- citation_style = apa: Cite in APA style.

## Allowed only with a written reason
Write the reason in docs/decisions/ before using any of these:
- Changing the citation style.
- Splitting, merging or reordering chapters.
- Editing the institution template.

## Design patterns
- No pattern without a named, concrete problem and a decision record in docs/decisions/.
- Write the direct solution first. Add a pattern when the same problem shows up again.
- Patterns that fit this profile: none listed for this profile. Cards: https://github.com/SVN11X/standards/tree/v1/patterns

## Avoid AI slop
- No comments that restate the code, narrate steps or decorate (banners, emoji).
- No speculative abstractions, dead code in what you write, unused dependencies or leftover placeholder data.
- No feature, option or error handling that nobody asked for or that covers a case that cannot happen.
- No fabricated content. Statistics, testimonials, references and links must be real and verified.
- No marketing words (seamless, cutting-edge, revolutionary, game-changer, supercharge).
- Plain prose. Short sentences, no filler openers, no em dashes or semicolons as separators.

## Owner preferences
- Use plain words. Explain a technical term briefly the first time it appears.
- Do not use em dashes or semicolons as separators. Use periods and commas.
- Reply in the language the owner writes in. Write every repository artifact in English.
